headline: Granted Certificate of Appropriateness for awning at 30 Central Street
summary: The commission approved the June 25, 2026 minutes and granted a Certificate of Appropriateness and Design Review for a black and white striped awning at 30 Central Street, Paloma Gifts storefront, through a series of findings motions. The commission also discussed adding character-defining features to historic district ordinance guidance and resources for applicants, with no formal action taken.
decisions: Approved finding that Part 2, Sections 3, 5, 6, and 8, and all of part three, be struck for irrelevance.
Approved finding that the application was deemed complete on July 9, 2026, is a Certificate of Appropriateness and Design Review, and fees were paid.
Approved finding that the application satisfies Historic Preservation Code §148-9A on preserving or enhancing historical and architectural character.
Approved finding that the application satisfies Historic Preservation Code §148-9B(2)(a) on providing compatible use with minimum alteration.
Approved finding that the application satisfies Historic Preservation Code §148-9B(2)(b) on not destroying distinguishing qualities or character.
Approved finding that the application satisfies Historic Preservation Code §148-9B(2)(d) on not damaging or destroying distinctive stylistic features.
Approved finding that the application satisfies Historic Preservation Code §148-9B(2)(g) on compatible contemporary design.
Approved finding that the application satisfies Historic Preservation Code §148-9B(2)(i) on preserving original structure integrity if alterations are removed.
Granted the Certificate of Appropriateness and Design Review Permit for the project at 30 Central Street.

decision_evidence.quote: Commissioner Sachs moved that the Commission finds that Part 2, Sections 3, 5, 6, and 8, as well as the entirety of part three, be struck for irrelevance. Commissioner Krupke seconded. All voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed.

Commissioner Sachs moved that the Commission finds that the application was deemed complete on July 9, 2026, the proposed project is a Certificate of Appropriateness and Design Review, and the applicant paid all applicable fees. Commissioner Krupke seconded. All voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed.

Commissioner Sachs moved that the Commission finds that, based on Exhibits 1 and 4, the application satisfied Historic Preservation Code §148-9A requiring that any alteration of the historic structure will preserve or enhance its historical and architectural character. Commissioner Krupke seconded. All voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed.

Commissioner Sachs moved that the Commission finds that, based on Exhibits 1 and 4, the application satisfies Historic Preservation Code § 148-9B(2)(a) requiring that every reasonable effort shall be made to provide a compatible use which will require minimum alteration to the structure and its environment. Commissioner Krupke seconded. All voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed.

Commissioner Sachs moved that the Commission finds that, based on Exhibits 1 and 4, the application satisfies Historic Preservation Code §148-9B(2)(b) requiring that rehabilitation work does not destroy the distinguishing qualities nor character of the structure and its environment. Commissioner Krupke seconded. All voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed.

Commissioner Sachs moved that the Commission finds that, based on Exhibits 1 and 4, the application satisfies Historic Preservation Code §148-9B(2)(d) requiring that distinctive stylistic features or examples of skilled craftsmanship which characterize historic structures is not damaged or destroyed, wherever possible. Commissioner Krupke seconded. All voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed.

Commissioner Sachs moved that the Commission finds that, based on Exhibits 1 and 4, the application satisfies Historic Preservation Code § 148-9B(2)(g) requiring contemporary design for additions to only be approved if such design is compatible with the size, scale, material, and character of the neighborhood, structures, or its environment. Commissioner Krupke seconded. All voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed.

Commissioner Sachs moved that the Commission finds that, based on Exhibits 1 and 4, the application satisfies Historic Preservation Code § 148-9B(2)(i) requiring that, wherever possible, all alterations to structures shall be done in such a manner that if they were to be removed in the future the essential form and integrity of the original structure would be unimpaired. Commissioner Krupke seconded. All voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed.

Commissioner Sachs moved that the Commission finds that, based on the findings in Parts 1-2 of Section IV of this document, the Project meets the requirements for a Certificate of Appropriateness and therefore grants a Certificate of Appropriateness and Design Review Permit for the proposed Project. Commissioner Krupke seconded. All voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed.

Historic Preservation Commission – Meeting Minutes 
July 9th, 2026 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
HISTORIC PRESERVATION COMMISSION 
MEETING OF JULY 9, 2026, 7:00 P.M. 
 COUNCIL CHAMBERS, CITY HALL 
73 HARLOW STREET  
 
 
MEETING MINUTES  
 
Commission Members Present:   Nathaniel King 
Rebecca Krupke 
Peter Sachs    
  
             
City Staff Present: Anne Krieg, Director of Community & 
Economic Development  
Matt Altiero, Planning Analyst 
Kayleigh Rienas, Development Assistant 
Mike Pullen, HPC Consultant 
 
Chair King called the meeting to order at 7:00 P.M. 
______________________________________________________________________ 
 
Old Business: 
1. Meeting Minutes -  June 25, 2026  
 
Commissioner Krupke moved to approve the June 25th meeting minutes. Commissioner Sachs 
seconded. All voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
  
New Business: 
 
2. Certificate of Appropriateness and Design Review – 30 Central Street – Map-Lot 
041-066 – Great Fire Historic District – Applicant: Rebeca Garcia Owner: Betsy 
Lundy- The applicant, Rebeca Garcia, requests approval for Certificate of 
Appropriateness and Design Review at property located at 30 Central Street for the 
addition of a black and white striped awning to Paloma Gifts storefront. The property is 
located at Map-Lot 041-066, in the Great Fire Historic District. Applicant: Rebeca Garcia. 
Owner: Betsy Lundy. 
 
Chair King introduced the agenda item.
Historic Preservation Commission – Meeting Minutes 
July 9th, 2026 
Applicant Rebeca Garcia presented to the podium. 
 
HPC Consultant Pullen discussed the building’s history, sharing that it was constructed in 1911 as part 
of the Frey, Dugan, Staples Block designed by Victor Hodgins and is one of the few buildings downtown 
clad in terracotta. 
 
HPC Consultant Pullen asked if the proposed awning is intended to be mounted above or below the sign 
band – Applicant Garcia clarified below the sign band. Community and Economic Development Director 
Krieg clarified that the awning will need to have a clearance of 8 feet. 
 
HPC Consultant Pullen asked if the terracotta was to remain white, but noted he observed a more 
recent photo displaying the storefront terracotta as black – Applicant Garcia confirmed it had been 
painted black. 
 
Chair King asked the Commission for any questions and discussion. 
 
Commissioner Krupke asked about whether terracotta risks being cracked or damaged by awning 
installation – HPC Consultant Pullen explained that, so long as the fasteners are installed in the mortar 
joints between blocks and not the face of the blocks, the terracotta will be preserved. 
 
Commissioner Krupke asked if a remaining white spot was to be painted black – Applicant Garcia 
confirmed. 
 
Commissioner Krupke discussed that awnings have been historically present downtown, so she 
supports the project. Chair King expressed he believes the colors selected will match the storefront well. 
Commissioner Sachs shared he appreciates the shade awnings provide downtown. 
 
Commissioner Sachs moved that the Commission finds that Part 2, Sections 3, 5, 6, and 8, as well as 
the entirety of part three, be struck for irrelevance. Commissioner Krupke seconded. All voting members 
in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Commissioner Sachs moved that the Commission finds that the application was deemed complete on 
July 9, 2026, the proposed project is a Certificate of Appropriateness and Design Review, and the 
applicant paid all applicable fees. Commissioner Krupke seconded. All voting members in favor, none 
opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Commissioner Sachs moved that the Commission finds that, based on Exhibits 1 and 4, the application 
satisfied Historic Preservation Code §148-9A requiring that any alteration of the historic structure will 
preserve or enhance its historical and architectural character. Commissioner Krupke seconded. All 
voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Commissioner Sachs moved that the Commission finds that, based on Exhibits 1 and 4, the application 
satisfies Historic Preservation Code § 148-9B(2)(a) requiring that every reasonable effort shall be made 
to provide a compatible use which will require minimum alteration to the structure and its environment. 
Commissioner Krupke seconded. All voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Commissioner Sachs moved that the Commission finds that, based on Exhibits 1 and 4, the application 
satisfies Historic Preservation Code §148-9B(2)(b) requiring that rehabilitation work does not destroy the 
distinguishing qualities nor character of the structure and its environment. Commissioner Krupke 
seconded. All voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Commissioner Sachs moved that the Commission finds that, based on Exhibits 1 and 4, the application
Historic Preservation Commission – Meeting Minutes 
July 9th, 2026 
satisfies Historic Preservation Code §148-9B(2)(d) requiring that distinctive stylistic features or 
examples of skilled craftsmanship which characterize historic structures is not damaged or destroyed, 
wherever possible. Commissioner Krupke seconded. All voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion 
passed. 
 
Commissioner Sachs moved that the Commission finds that, based on Exhibits 1 and 4, the 
application satisfies Historic Preservation Code § 148-9B(2)(g) requiring contemporary design for 
additions to only be approved if such design is compatible with the size, scale, material, and 
character of the neighborhood, structures, or its environment. Commissioner Krupke seconded. All 
voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Commissioner Sachs moved that the Commission finds that, based on Exhibits 1 and 4, the 
application satisfies Historic Preservation Code § 148-9B(2)(i) requiring that, wherever possible, all 
alterations to structures shall be done in such a manner that if they were to be removed in the future 
the essential form and integrity of the original structure would be unimpaired. Commissioner Krupke 
seconded. All voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Commissioner Sachs moved that the Commission finds that, based on the findings in Parts 1-2 of 
Section IV of this document, the Project meets the requirements for a Certificate of Appropriateness and 
therefore grants a Certificate of Appropriateness and Design Review Permit for the proposed Project. 
Commissioner Krupke seconded. All voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
3. Discuss Character-Defining Features in the Historic Districts 
 
HPC Consultant Pullen recommended Commissioners acquire A Field Guide to American Architecture 
by Virginia McAlester to reference styles when reviewing applications. He recommended adding 
character-defining features to ordinance definitions. 
 
HPC Consultant Pullen referenced §148-9.B.2.b, stating: “Rehabilitation work shall not destroy the 
distinguishing qualities nor character of the structure and its environment.” Additionally, he referenced 
the Secretary of Interior’s Standards for Rehabilitation and Guidelines for Rehabilitation, stating: “A 
prominent or distinctive aspect, quality, or characteristic of a historic property that contributes 
significantly to its physical character. Structures, objects, vegetation, spatial relationships, views, 
furnishings, decorative details, and materials may be such features.” 
 
HPC Consultant Pullen discussed including character-defining features in the ordinance as reference 
materials for applicants and a standard for the Commission. He recommended reviewing the Secretary 
of Interior’s resources for support.   
 
HPC Consultant Pullen expressed how some history-rich buildings were not protected, and are therefore 
irretrievable. He shared that after the Great Fire of 1911, the City prioritized fire resistance and created 
buildings with architectural significance. He discussed that historic architectural drawings often were not 
preserved or recorded, as linen was utilized for drawings, and the ink would be wiped off for reuse. 
 
Community and Economic Development Director Krieg shared that as staff explores improvements to 
the code, direction from the Commission is useful to understand what may be most helpful for 
applicants. She discussed revisiting the application form to see if there is an avenue to provide more 
information. HPC Consultant Pullen recommended referring applicants to the standards the Commission 
reviews by and asking them to prepare a presentation relative to how their project meets those 
standards -- Commissioner Krupke clarified something similar to a step by step guide. Pullen suggested 
asking applicants what historic district the project is located in rather than zoning district.
Historic Preservation Commission – Meeting Minutes 
July 9th, 2026 
HPC Consultant Pullen commented that window projects may be complicated, as windows of varying 
size change the characteristics of the window and building.  
 
Commissioner Krupke expressed she agrees with the suggestions, as future Commission members may 
not have a vested interest in historic homes or related field of education, highlighting the importance of 
guidelines.  
 
Community and Economic Development Director Krieg discussed letters sent to new owners within 
historic districts, noting potentially including more information about the significance of the particular 
district. HPC Consultant Pullen discussed the possibility of including Cultural and Architectural Resource 
Management Archive forms attached to the letter. Commissioner Krupke recommended adding 
something eye-catching to increase readership, such as sharing what makes their building special. Krieg 
noted that the new generation of buyers or residents moving in from elsewhere may not know the 
significance of a neighborhood. 
 
Chair King suggested adding the Commission presentations surrounding architectural styles and 
character-defining features to the City webpage as a resource for applicants. He discussed the potential 
of a story map that displays examples of architectural styles by district and includes the associated 
character-defining features. King recommended creating a handout and collection of reference materials 
for future Commission members – HPC Consultant Pullen agreed that would be useful. Commissioner 
Sachs agreed, expressing not everyone has a background in historic preservation. 
 
Chair King asked if the Commission should consider indirect effects to historic districts and structures, 
such as developments that alter the viewshed. HPC Consultant Pullen responded that the City of 
Portland has developed guidelines for when the line of a façade extends upwards, and noted that there 
have not been many instances of applicants constructing above existing rooftops in Bangor. Pullen 
commented that even when additions may not be visible from the sidewalk, they are still visible in the 
viewshed.  
 
HPC Consultant Pullen shared that pre-application meetings have been useful to provide overviews to 
applicants and discuss potential issues. Community and Economic Development Director Krieg added it 
is helpful to engage in such processes at a staff level with Pullen present. Pullen noted it aids in the 
applicant’s preparedness. Chair King expressed it would be helpful to have a handout to discuss the 
style of a home, discuss what the character-defining features are, and discuss how to mitigate the loss 
of that feature.  
 
Commissioner Krupke asked about the address list present in the meeting materials – Community and 
Economic Development Director Krieg clarified it is an abutters list to the proposed project at 30 Central 
Street. 
 
4. Adjournment 
 
Meeting adjourned at 8:01 PM.  
 
Respectfully submitted,  
 
Kayleigh Rienas 
Development Assistant 
Planning Division
